PE and Sports Premium
The government is providing funding of £150 million to provide new and substantial primary school sport funding. The funding is being jointly provided by the Departments for Education, Health and Culture, and Media and Sport, and will see money going directly to primary school headteachers to spend on improving the quality of sport and PE for all their children.
This funding is intended for the purposes of establishing and developing sports activities which are sustainable in the long term.
Academic Year 2024/2025
The Department of Education has changed the way schools report their sports funding this year. The system used is online and produces summary files which can be found below.
In essence, we spend the sports funding to support the key areas that we feel are important to the children. These include:
Continuous Professional Development of staff including training a new Forest School Leader, PE Conference for the new PE Leader, Get Set for PE whole school planning package.
Swimming - catchup lessons for the children in Year 5.
Internal Opportunities such as the delivery of Forest School, after school clubs and external cricket clubs in Early Years and Key Stage 1.
Equipment renewal for OPAL and PE lessons.

Public Consultation to reinstate the Nursery provision to full time
Public Consultation to reinstate the Nursery provision to full time.
School: The Ridgeway Primary School (Church Ward)
Local authority: Reading Borough Council, Civic Offices, Bridge St, Reading RG1 2LU
The Governing Body of The Ridgeway Primary School intends to reinstate 26 afternoon (PM) places for 3‑ and 4‑year‑olds with effect from Thursday 3rd September 2026. This builds on the 26 morning (AM) places already offered, enabling the school to support 30-hour provision, term time for working families.
Description of alteration
To maximise the use of the existing nursery classroom space, staff, and resources during the afternoon session.
Effect on other provisions within the area
Our intention is to enhance the Nursery offer at The Ridgeway to parents choosing us for the primary education of their children. We do not anticipate that this will have a negative impact on other nursery providers in the area. The introduction of an afternoon, school-based nursery offer will provide greater flexibility and opportunity for families seeking full-day arrangements in South Reading.
Our objectives are to provide all day nursery arrangements for working families, enabling access to extended childcare hours that support employment, training, and financial stability. We believe that this will strengthen children’s transition to reception by delivering a high‑quality curriculum and teaching that builds strong foundations for all children. Our aim is to provide free, accessible places that promote equity and remove financial barriers for all families. Having the extended nursery hours will support continuity of education and care through to school where this is parental preference and allocated through the admissions process.
There are no additional costs to the school in relation to the changes as staffing and facilities are already in place.
We intend to implement this to start in September 2026 and will communicate with existing parents who have morning only places as well as market our new offer to working parents who are choosing The Ridgeway Primary school.
Within four weeks from the date of publication of this proposal, any person may object to, support or make comments on the proposal by completing the following online form:
https://forms.cloud.microsoft/e/D6Lv3wFfKy
If you would like a printed copy of the form please contact the Office Manager details below.
If you have any questions relating to this proposal, please contact Rachel Wiggins the Office Manager at the Ridgeway Primary School either by phone (0118 937 5530) or email (officemanager@theridgeway.reading.sch.uk).
Responses will be shared with:
Publication Date: Tuesday 14th April 2026
Closing Date for Response: Tuesday 12th May 2026

Rights Respecting School
The Rights Respecting Schools Award puts children’s rights at the heart of school life in the UK.
The UK Committee for UNICEF (UNICEF UK) works with schools in the UK to create safe and inspiring places to learn, where children are respected, their talents are nurtured and they are able to thrive.
Our Rights Respecting Schools Award embeds these values in daily school life and gives children the best chance to lead happy, healthy lives and to be responsible, active citizens.
Over 1.7 million children in the UK go to a Rights Respecting School and over 5,000 schools up and down the country are working through the Award.
The Award recognises a school’s achievement in putting the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child into practice within the school and beyond.

Meet the Governors
Norah Edgar Governor (Head Teacher)
Corrinne Hackett Co-opted Governor (Assistant Headteacher)
Suzanne Ismail Co-opted Governor, Co-Chair of Governors and Chair of Resources Committee
Mary Lewis Staff Governor (Teaching Staff)
Shazia Sheikh Parent Governor
Shazia is a parent of seven children ranging from 2 to 24 years. She has home educated her children over the last 20 years whilst completing a BA Hons degree in Childhood and Youth Studies with the Open University. She has worked as a Triple P Practitioner and Facilitator helping parents with their children's behavioural issues and found this experience to be very rewarding indeed. Shazia has also ran an array of community clubs such as: Parent and Toddlers, Sports Clubs and Home Education clubs over the last 20 years. Shazia hopes to bring her wealth of experience gained from working with a variety of families to her role of Parent Governor in a quest to help improve the lives of everyone connected with The Ridgeway Primary School.
Ruth McEwan Local Authority Governor
Dan Mead Co-opted Governor, Co-Chair of Governors
Dan is a lifelong Reading resident, from being born in the Royal Berkshire Hospital to going to school across the road at Reading School, and now living in the Borough. He is currently a civil servant at His Majesty's Treasury where he is an economist monitoring the financial health of the corporate sector. He also previously held positions in the Department for Levelling Up, Housing and Communities. Dan believes that education, particularly the early years of school, is incredibly important and hopes to help The Ridgeway Primary School give every person the best possible start to life.
Jessica del Rio Parent Governor
Jessica has 20+ years experience working in a higher education environment, and is currently working across the project management and change management teams at The University of Reading. She has a particular interest in equality of opportunity in education for all children, regardless of circumstance and also in how mental and physical wellness contribute to effective learning. Jessica has three children at Ridgeway Primary
If you would like to contact any member of the governing board, please contact Lorraine Doyle, Governance Officer via Clerk@theridgeway.reading.sch.uk
Ambika Paranthaman, Co-opted Governor
Ambika has lived in Reading since 2023 after relocating from India to the UK. She is a Data Science Lead at CGI, with extensive experience in data science, technology, leadership, and strategic decision-making. Prior to moving to the UK, she worked in Indian universities, teaching and mentoring students in technology-related disciplines, which gave her valuable insight into education and student development. She has experience across both academia and industry, contributing to research, teaching, and real-world applications.
In addition to her professional career, Ambika serves as a Foundation Director of a school in London, contributing to governance, strategic planning, and organisational improvement. As a parent of a non-verbal child with special educational needs, she has a strong personal commitment to inclusion, accessibility, and ensuring that every child has the opportunity to thrive.
she is passionate about supporting education and community development. She is keen to use her professional expertise, governance experience, and commitment to inclusive education to contribute positively to the school's leadership and help support its continued success and long-term vision.
